title: Contraction of a field complex onto its single cohomology
statement: Let R be a field and P an integer-indexed cochain complex of module sheaves on Spec R [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-derived-category]. For an integer j, suppose H^q(P) is zero for every integer q different from j. Then P is homotopy equivalent to the single complex on its actual homology sheaf H^j(P) in degree j. No boundedness, local freeness, rank or basis is assumed.

source.place: Proof step 4; vector-space splitting spelled out in lem-pc-finite-free-single-field-fibre proof step 2.

proof.text: Apply moduleSpecΓFunctor, an additive equivalence from module sheaves on a field spectrum to R-vector spaces. It preserves homology. Write V_n for the term, Z_n for cycles and B_n for boundaries. Choose vector-space complements H_n of B_n inside Z_n and C_n of Z_n inside V_n. Then V_n=B_n⊕H_n⊕C_n; projection Z_n→H_n identifies H_n with the homology in degree n.

The differential restricts to an isomorphism C_n→B_(n+1). Define the homotopy V_n→V_(n-1) to be its inverse on B_n, and zero on H_n and C_n. Projection onto H_n and inclusion of H_n are chain maps. On B_n, d h is the identity and h d is zero; on C_n, h d is the identity and d h is zero; on H_n both are zero. Thus d h+h d=id-inclusion∘projection, whereas projection∘inclusion=id.

The assumed homology vanishing for all integer degrees other than j forces the corresponding H_n summands to be zero. Identify H_j with the actual homology, giving a homotopy equivalence to its single complex in degree j. Transport maps and the two homotopies along the inverse global-sections equivalence and its unit isomorphism. Naturality of the unit and preservation of compositions and sums establish the same identities for sheaves. This argument is degreewise and applies to unbounded or acyclic complexes too.
